Class AbstractHttpClient<R extends ByteBodyHttpResponse<?>>

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.http.client.AbstractHttpClient<R>
Type Parameters:
R - The type of a raw response of the transport, whose body bytes are not read yet
All Implemented Interfaces:
LifeCycle<HttpClient>, HttpClient, SseClient, StreamingHttpClient, Closeable, AutoCloseable
Direct Known Subclasses:
DefaultJdkHttpClient
@Internal public abstract class AbstractHttpClient<R extends ByteBodyHttpResponse<?>> extends Object implements HttpClient, StreamingHttpClient, SseClient
The part of an HTTP client that does not depend on its transport: the state of the client, the resolution of the request URI and the load balancing, the filters and the redirects, the decoding of streamed elements and events, and the reactive, blocking and asynchronous views of the exchanges. A transport sends one request and produces the raw response, see send(PropagatedContext, AtomicReference, Thread, MutableHttpRequest, LoadBalancerSelection), and builds a response whose body is fully read, see fullResponse(Argument, Argument, R, CloseableAvailableByteBody).
Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • send

      protected abstract ExecutionFlow<R> send(PropagatedContext propagatedContext, AtomicReference<ScheduledExecutorService> preferredScheduler, @Nullable Thread blockedThread, MutableHttpRequest<?> request, @Nullable LoadBalancerSelection selection)
      Send one request, without filters and without following redirects.
      Parameters:
      propagatedContext - The context propagated from the original client call
      preferredScheduler - A reference holding the preferred scheduler for timeouts, which the transport may replace with the one of its connection
      blockedThread - The thread that blocks on the response, if any
      request - The request to send, with a resolved absolute URI
      selection - The selection of the load balancer for the request, or null
      Returns:
      The flow of the raw response, whose body bytes are not read yet

    • sendBuffered

      protected ExecutionFlow<R> sendBuffered(PropagatedContext propagatedContext, AtomicReference<ScheduledExecutorService> preferredScheduler, @Nullable Thread blockedThread, MutableHttpRequest<?> request, @Nullable LoadBalancerSelection selection, AtomicBoolean headersReceived)
      Send one request of an exchange whose response body is read whole, see readFullResponse(R, Argument, Argument, Function), without filters and without following redirects: a transport may read the body into memory right away. By default, see send(PropagatedContext, AtomicReference, Thread, MutableHttpRequest, LoadBalancerSelection).
      Parameters:
      propagatedContext - The context propagated from the original client call
      preferredScheduler - A reference holding the preferred scheduler for timeouts, which the transport may replace with the one of its connection
      blockedThread - The thread that blocks on the response, if any
      request - The request to send, with a resolved absolute URI
      selection - The selection of the load balancer for the request, or null
      headersReceived - Set by a transport that reads the body before the flow completes, once the response headers arrived: a timeout of the exchange then elapsed while the body was read
      Returns:
      The flow of the raw response

    • sendRequestWithRedirects

      protected ExecutionFlow<HttpResponse<?>> sendRequestWithRedirects(PropagatedContext propagatedContext, AtomicReference<ScheduledExecutorService> preferredScheduler, @Nullable Thread blockedThread, MutableHttpRequest<?> request, @Nullable LoadBalancerSelection selection, BiFunction<MutableHttpRequest<?>, R, ? extends ExecutionFlow<? extends HttpResponse<?>>> readResponse)
      This is the high-level request method. It sits above send(PropagatedContext, AtomicReference, Thread, MutableHttpRequest, LoadBalancerSelection) and handles things like filters, redirects and response parsing.
      Parameters:
      propagatedContext - The context propagated from the original client call
      preferredScheduler - A reference holding the preferred scheduler for timeouts. This is replaced by the transport ASAP so that callers can take advantage of locality
      blockedThread - The thread that blocks on the response, if any
      request - The request to send. Must have resolved absolute URI (see resolveRequestURI(HttpRequest))
      selection - The selection of the load balancer for the request, or null if the request was not load balanced. It is released when the exchange ends without reporting an outcome
      readResponse - Function that reads the response from the raw response. This is run exactly once, but if there is a redirect, it potentially runs with a different request than the original (which is why it has a request parameter)
      Returns:
      A flow containing the response

    • exchangeEventStream

      public <I,B> Publisher<HttpResponse<Event<B>>> exchangeEventStream(HttpRequest<I> request, Argument<B> eventType, Argument<?> errorType)
      Description copied from interface: SseClient

      Perform an HTTP request whose response is either a stream of SSE Event objects or a single body, and receive each event wrapped in an HttpResponse that exposes the response status and headers.

      This suits protocols where the server decides per request whether to answer with a single body or with text/event-stream, such as the MCP Streamable HTTP transport:

      • The Accept header of the request is kept when it accepts text/event-stream, for example application/json, text/event-stream. Otherwise text/event-stream is added to it.
      • When the content type of the response is text/event-stream, the body is decoded as events, and each event is emitted as soon as it arrives. The data of each event is decoded as JSON into the event type.
      • Otherwise the whole body is decoded into the event type, using the content type of the response, and emitted as a single event.
      • When the body holds no event, for example a 202 Accepted response, a single response without a body is emitted, so the status and headers are always available.
      • When the response has an error status, the publisher fails with an HttpClientResponseException carrying the response and its body, decoded into the error type.

      The downstream Subscriber can regulate demand via the subscription

      Specified by:
      exchangeEventStream in interface SseClient
      Type Parameters:
      I - The request body type
      B - The event body type
      Parameters:
      request - The HttpRequest to execute
      eventType - The event data type
      errorType - The type that the response body should be coerced into if the server responds with an error
      Returns:
      A Publisher that emits the events of the response, each wrapped in an HttpResponse
